target_customer: Patients with heart conditions and physicians who prescribe ambulatory ECG monitoring
problem: Patients at risk of heart events lack an affordable device for continuous at-home monitoring that can also call for emergency help.
business_model: Medical hardware device sold to patients and physicians; later a clinical-grade ECG monitor

founders.name: Andre Bertram
education: Danforth Collegiate high school, Toronto (Grade 12 student in 2015)
founders.background_notes: Youth Basecamp Program at Ryerson Brookfield Institute in 2015.

founders.name: Frank Nguyen
education: Danforth Collegiate high school, Toronto (Grade 12 student in 2015)
founders.background_notes: Came up with the idea, inspired by his mother's health problems. Not listed on the YC page; named co-founder by the student newspaper and a University of Waterloo news item.

technical_complexity.rationale: A medical-grade wearable with ECG sensing, cellular emergency calling and GPS needs hardware, firmware and regulatory clearance, hard for two teenage founders.

defensibility.rationale: Regulatory clearance could protect a shipped product, but at founding there was no clearance and consumer wearables could copy features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Smartwatch ECG became common after 2018 per general sources; no source ties an incumbent action directly to HelpWear.

market_need_then: Aging population and heart disease burden; the founders stated they wanted to avoid reliance on cellphones or Bluetooth for emergency calling (student newspaper, 2015).

identity.logo: Described by an aggregator as a blue pulse on white; not confirmed from brand materials
identity.voice_and_tone: Site says 'Innovating Hardware to Empower Telemedicine'

branding.community_and_virality: Dragons' Den TV appearance in 2017 drew press from the University of Waterloo and Toronto outlets.

brand_strength.rationale: Teen founders and a TV appearance drew local press, but no evidence of a broad brand following.

outcome_analysis: HelpWear is still active with a Toronto office but appears to be at a pilot stage per a University of Calgary portfolio page, years after the 2017 batch. Funding stayed small, mostly competitions, grants and a Dragons' Den deal, and the hardware regulatory path is slow, so the company has stalled short of a venture outcome so far.
notes: Dragons' Den: asked 100K USD for 10 percent, reports say 12 percent was given (trimech blog and an aggregator); equity figure not recorded. Unverified: aggregator reports a 100K USD J&J QuickFire grant in 2021 and about 250K USD seed in 2022 (NEXT Founders, Faktory Ventures, L-SPARK); no primary source. Competitor searches returned only undated or current aggregator pages, so no dated competitor list was built. The round stage is other because sources do not label it.
